task.description: WF-03 Step 4a SECURITY-REVIEWER hard gate (.claude/agents/security-reviewer.md; docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8). This is test-support code, not a runtime tenant-data path, but it is a SECURITY-REVIEWER F2 follow-up, so review it as the guard it is: can the guard be bypassed or fail open (empty/nil config, prefix like letflow_test_prod_copy, :expected_database seam abuse, fresh-clone and TenantTemplate paths left unguarded, partition suffix, case sensitivity, current_database() read on a sandboxed connection, Sandbox shared-mode edge), does it run before every destructive side effect reachable from start_pool!/2 and from a direct GenServer.start of the Pool, does it add any secret/log leak (database names in messages are acceptable), does anything reach lib/ or production. Verify the test seam cannot weaken production. Verdict with BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR findings. Q-1054 / GH #2400 (queue ref ISS-1054, local record docs/issues/ISS-1061.yaml), branch feature/WF03-ISS1054DBGUARD-20261012, implementation commit c4944af4a (step 03 handoff). Change: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex adds assert_test_database!/1 (expected name from Repo.config()[:database], letflow_test* prefix check, current_database() equality, ArgumentError, fail closed), called in start_pool!/2 after Sandbox.mode(:auto) and before GenServer.start/create_slots, plus defense in depth in Pool.init/1; new :expected_database test seam; tests T1..T5 in test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs; test/specs/ISS-1061.md; one paragraph in lib/letflow/design/iss1042-pooled-tenant-fixture.md. Compare with `git diff origin/main...HEAD`. Design: step-01 and validator step-02b handoffs under handoffs/WF03-ISS1054DBGUARD-20261012/. No mix needed (all gates already ran; if you want to run any mix use the mutex: L=/c/Users/tvolo/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/mixlock; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$L")"; until mkdir "$L" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 20; done; trap 'rmdir "$L" 2>/dev/null' EXIT; cd /c/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow && LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5499 MIX_ENV=test <ONE mix invocation>, with a throwaway postgres:16 on 5499 you remove afterwards). Foreground only, no Monitors. Result into your handoff (COMPLETED, result.status PASS/FAIL, no BOM, LF, no self-reference in artifacts_out); pull --rebase, commit, push with bounded retry; message ends 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>'. Concurrent sibling gate writes another handoff on this branch: pull --rebase before push.

result.summary: SECURITY-REVIEWER Step 4a PASS. Scope: test-support code only (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, test, spec, one design-doc paragraph); no lib/ runtime code, no migration, no secret/route/response-shaping change; test/support is compiled only under MIX_ENV=test (mix.exs elixirc_paths), the only lib/ diff is a markdown design doc. INV-1/2/3/5/6/9/10 NOT-APPLICABLE; INV-4 (no secret read, only the database NAME in error text, which the task accepts), INV-7 (single literal SELECT current_database(), no interpolation) and INV-8 (raise is the intended fail-closed refusal in test setup) PASS. Guard analysis: (1) fails closed on nil/empty/non-binary config (is_binary and starts_with check raises); (2) case-sensitive, LetFlow_test refused; (3) partition suffix letflow_test2 accepted as intended; (4) :expected_database seam can only narrow, never widen: value must start with letflow_test AND equal current_database(), so passing the real DB name is a no-op and any other value is refused; production cannot reach it (not in lib/, no release path); (5) ordering: before the guard start_pool! performs only argument validation and Sandbox.mode(:auto), no DB write; guard runs before GenServer.start and create_slots, so refusal leaves nothing to tear down; (6) direct GenServer.start of Pool is covered by init/1 re-assertion, which defaults to the configured DB when :expected_database is absent (Map.get nil), and a raising init returns {:error, ...} with no state; (7) current_database() is identical on sandboxed and auto connections, and the guard runs after mode(:auto); no Sandbox shared-mode edge since the query is read-only; (8) no new secret/log leak.

findings.text: The equality check is partly tautological: expected defaults to Repo.config()[:database], the same value the connection was opened with, so the letflow_test* prefix is the effective control. A real database deliberately named letflow_test_prod_copy and configured as the Repo database would pass. Acceptable for a naming-convention guard; no change required.

Fresh-clone and Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate paths (provisioned_tenant!/1, ensure_template!, reaper) remain unguarded; explicitly declared out of scope in the moduledoc and design note. Consider a follow-up issue if the same destructive-DROP protection is wanted there.
